answer: Each applicant posts a 50 nectar bond on the timber register for a five-juror panel to review. Jurors drawn from the reef pool stake 20 nectar each; a majority verdict admits or rejects, and a proven fake burns its bond and approving jurors' stakes. Running 1,000 fakes risks 50,000 nectar; the k-th fake still pays 50 nectar plus a panel slot, as one juror sits at most three panels per epoch. Bribing fails: the draw is random and hidden until verdict, and a dissenting juror keeps its stake plus a share of the seized bond. An honest agent posts one 50 nectar bond, recovered after a clean epoch.
